newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian food processor says no news on equity cut.
newsitem.headline: Croatian food processor says no news on equity cut.

text.p: Croatian food-processing firm Podravka d.d. said on Thursday it was still waiting for the government to rule on its proposed equity cut as a necessary step in further restructuring and privatisation.
"We have had no reply yet from the Privatisation Fund, which should give a final approval," Ivan Slabek, secretary of the company board, told Reuters by telephone.
Podravka, based in Koprivnica in northern Croatia, said earlier this month it hoped to get the ruling before its annual shareholders' meeting on September 27.

The company had asked the state privatisation agency to reduce its capital by an estimated 124 million German marks from the government stake, after independent auditors found its total capital of 524 million overvalued by that amount.
After such a move, private ownership by some 17,000 small shareholders would be raised to 47 percent from the current 39 percent.

A similar model was applied in privatisation of drugs firm Pliva, which then floated its shares abroad. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) bought an 11-percent stake in the company to speed up its sell-off.
Market rumours about Podravka's negotiations with the EBRD have recently pushed its share price to 250 kuna, or over 70 percent of face value, from under 50 percent a few months ago.
But the company denied last week that a deal was anywhere near being struck and declined to comment on the course of talks.

Podravka made a group loss of 135.3 million kuna for 1995 because of high costs of borrowing, production losses at some of its subsidiaries and depressed food prices. It also blamed an overvalued kuna for putting a lid on exports.
